name: layout17
description: Adaptive Korean campus-fresh editorial collage with a phone screen / digital scrapbook UI aesthetic. Before composing this layout, analyze the first uploaded image and extract three things: (1) dominant color palette — identify the 2–3 hero colors and 1–2 accent tones present in the outfit; (2) outfit aesthetic/mood — classify the overall vibe (e.g. preppy/campus, soft feminine, streetwear, dark academic, cottagecore, etc.); (3) outfit motif or texture — identify any recurring pattern or material quality (gingham, lace, knit, plaid, floral, leather, solid, etc.). Color rule: all UI elements, decorative graphic colors, card border tints, and overlay accents must use a complementary or contrasting palette relative to the outfit's dominant color — not the same hue (e.g. navy gingham outfit → warm blush or soft terracotta UI accents; cream lace outfit → muted sage or dusty lavender; black outfit → warm off-white or amber). Complementary contrast should feel fresh and campus-bright — harmonious opposites, not garish clashes. Background is determined by the outfit aesthetic and vibe detected from the first uploaded image — choose a background environment that best matches the mood (e.g. preppy/campus → bleacher or stadium tribune seats in school colors, slightly blurred; soft feminine → soft floral garden or pastel café interior, desaturated; streetwear → urban rooftop or concrete wall, slightly blurred; dark academic → library or cobblestone courtyard; cottagecore → open field or greenhouse); desaturate slightly and apply fine paper grain; if the vibe is ambiguous, use a clean muted solid in a complementary tone with fine paper grain. Layout structure mimics a phone screen: a simulated iOS or Android status/app-dock bar at top edge and navigation bar at bottom edge — both styled in a neutral complementary tone (white pill or rounded bar); photo cards arranged within this screen area: one small portrait card upper-left (thin border, slight tilt), one large portrait card upper-right (straight, thin border), one detail/close-up card mid-left (borderless or thin border, slight overlap), one large portrait card lower-right spanning toward center; if 5–6 photos available, add one more small card in the center gap or lower-left. Decorative graphic elements: derive element types from the aesthetic mood of the first uploaded image (e.g. preppy/campus → fresh green plant stem cutout, lace or ribbon fragment, varsity patch sticker; soft feminine → floral bloom cutouts, pastel ribbon, pearl accent; streetwear → bold sticker graphics, spray-texture marks, chain cutout; dark academic → quill or ink stamp, dried botanical, book page scrap; cottagecore → pressed flower, twine bow, mushroom cutout) — but render all element colors in the complementary/contrasting palette, not the outfit's own colors. Card borders in white or a light complementary tint. Typography overlays minimal, color from complementary palette. Clean Korean editorial styling, bright outdoor or studio daylight photography. Follow the phone-screen UI framing with inner scattered card arrangement; adapt slot count within the 4–6 range.
swipe_cta: Add a small UI-native swipe CTA element matching the phone-screen aesthetic (e.g. pill-shaped button or bottom-bar hint with 'Swipe →' or 'See more'). Color it in the complementary/contrasting palette relative to the outfit — not the outfit's own hue. If the extracted aesthetic is softer or more analog, render as a handwritten tag or washi tape strip instead, still in the complementary palette. Keep wording minimal (2–4 words). Position near the bottom navigation bar area.
